{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash -l

# Flux batch script (translated from Slurm)

# Slurm requested:
#   --gres=gpu:8
#   --cpus-per-task=5
#   --ntasks-per-node=8
#   --time=1-00:00
#   --job-name=openpsg
#   --output=.../%j.out

# In Flux, run an allocation then execute the job in it.
# -n: total tasks (ntasks). Slurm ntasks-per-node=8; node count unspecified, so request 8 tasks total.
# -c: cores per task (cpus-per-task)
# --gpus: total GPUs
# --time: walltime
# Output path: Flux supports output redirection; %j is replaced by Flux jobid using ${FLUX_JOB_ID}.

flux alloc \
  -n 8 \
  -c 5 \
  --gpus=8 \
  --time=24h \
  bash -lc '

# Best-effort job name: Flux does not have a portable "job name" directive in the batch script itself.
# Performance implication: none (metadata only), but it may affect how jobs are identified in queues/accounting.

echo "Flux Job ID: ${FLUX_JOB_ID}" 

# Redirect stdout/stderr to match Slurm --output (approximation)
# Slurm used: /jmain02/home/J2AD019/exk01/%u/logs/%j.out
# Use $USER for %u and ${FLUX_JOB_ID} for %j.
exec >"/jmain02/home/J2AD019/exk01/${USER}/logs/${FLUX_JOB_ID}.out" 2>&1

source ~/.bashrc
module load cuda
nvidia-smi -i ${CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES}
nvcc --version

CONFIG=$1
GPUS=8
PORT=$(shuf -i 10000-65535 -n 1)

export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:128

PYTHONPATH="$(dirname $0)/..":$PYTHONPATH \
EVAL_PAN_RELS=False \
WANDB_MODE="offline" \
python -m torch.distributed.launch \
  --nproc_per_node=$GPUS \
  --master_port=$PORT \
  tools/train.py \
  $CONFIG \
  --auto-resume \
  --no-validate \
  --seed 666 \
  --launcher pytorch
'

# Notes on omitted/approximate translations:
# - Slurm --ntasks-per-node=8: Flux request above uses -n 8 total tasks.
#   Without an explicit node count constraint, the scheduler may place these tasks across nodes.
#   Performance implication: if tasks span multiple nodes, distributed training may incur higher network overhead.
# - Slurm --job-name=openpsg: not expressed as a portable Flux batch directive here.
#   Performance implication: none; affects job labeling/monitoring only.
# - Slurm --output used %j substitution; Flux does not use the same token.
#   We approximate using ${FLUX_JOB_ID}; if your site uses different variables, logging may not land in the intended file.
"
}
